name: og_35_chemical_energy_coupling
description: Gate E energy coupling: does a specified thioester carrier cycle do endergonic work when the geochemical gradient DIPS, beating a matched gradient-only control, with a FULL closing energy ledger and no hidden inflow? carrier=True charges/discharges a stored carrier (buffered); carrier=False is the gradient-only null (direct drive->work, no store). Both see the same declining drive + load. Carrier chemistry = one specified thioester (Option B; acyl-phosphate / microkinetic = og-35a). Metabolism = sustained A1 network, NOT autocatalytic (A2 refuted).

carrier.description: Thioester carrier cycle (True) vs matched gradient-only null (False)

decline_rate.description: Drive decline per step (kJ/mol) — the gradient dip

base_CO2.description: Vent feed (provenance for the metabolic regime)

drive.doc:
The sustained environmental free-energy supply — the vent's geochemical /
redox disequilibrium that an early system could tap. Writes a (optionally
declining) exergonic drive free energy ΔG (kJ/mol) that the currency process
couples to. Steady by default; a decline models the gradient waning so the
store must carry the system through.

_contract.summary: Sustained environmental (geochemical) free-energy supply — an exergonic drive ΔG the proto-energy currency couples to.
_contract.description: Writes drive_free_energy = max(g_floor, g_drive - decline_rate * t), the per-transfer free energy (kJ/mol) available from the vent's redox / geochemical disequilibrium (e.g. FeS-mediated redox, H2/CO2). The currency process can only charge a carrier whose bond this drive can clear — so the drive ΔG sets which carriers are chargeable, not just how fast.

outputs.drive_free_energy: exergonic environmental drive ΔG available this tick (kJ/mol)

assumptions: A controlled environmental supply (not a scripted upgrade of the system).

engine.doc: Named thioester/acyl-phosphate carrier cycle with a closed free-energy ledger.

emitter.doc:
Generic Parquet emitter, hive-partitioned per ``partitioning_keys``.

The process-bigraph lifecycle drives the emit cadence:

  - configuration is written at ``__init__`` time from ``config["metadata"]``
    (only when ``metadata`` is non-None);
  - history rows arrive via ``update(state)`` per composite tick;
  - ``close(success=...)`` flushes the buffer and (when ``success=True``
    and a partitioning layout is configured) writes the success sentinel.

Durability-sensitive callers must call ``close()`` explicitly at end of
composite run; ``__del__`` calls it defensively but interpreter-shutdown
ordering is undefined.
